resources.string: Mail that lives on your own server.
No Croft account is needed. Your mail goes straight to your server.
We look up your server settings for you.
Enter your full email address, like name@example.org.
Enter a full email address to continue.
Croft checks these places at the same time.
the domain does not publish this
it took too long to answer
the network or name service could not be reached
the server\'s certificate was not accepted
the answer was not in a form Croft understands
the server sent Croft somewhere it does not follow
the domain offers only an unencrypted connection
If your server uses an app password, paste that here instead.
Gmail needs an app password or your own OAuth client until Croft\'s shared Google sign-in is verified. Create an app password in your Google account and paste it here.
Outlook and Microsoft 365 need an app password or your own OAuth client until Croft\'s shared Microsoft sign-in is verified. Create an app password in your Microsoft account and paste it here.
iCloud needs an app-specific password. Create one in your Apple ID account and paste it here.
Fastmail needs an app password. Create one in your Fastmail settings and paste it here.

Croft does not know who issued the security certificate of %1$s. It may be self-signed. Trust it only if you, or your organisation, set this server up, and the fingerprint below matches the one your server shows. Your password has not been sent.

The certificate of %1$s is not the one you trusted before. It may have been renewed, or someone may be intercepting your connection. Do not trust it unless the owner of the server confirms the new fingerprint below. Your password has not been sent.
Croft could not find your server\'s settings by itself. These are a guess: check them with your email provider.
Croft only connects over an encrypted connection.
Needed to send mail. You can leave it empty for now.
Enter the server name, like mail.example.org.
That is not a server name. Use letters, numbers, dots and hyphens, like mail.example.org.
Enter a port number from 1 to 65535.
Older mail keeps downloading in the background. You can start reading now.
The server stopped the first sync. You can still continue: Croft will tell you what to do in the inbox.
That does not look like an email address. Check it and try again.
Couldn\'t reach any server to look up %1$s. Check that you are online, then try again.
Croft couldn\'t find the settings for %1$s. You can enter them yourself.
Croft couldn\'t start looking up %1$s on this device. Try again in a moment.
Something went wrong inside Croft while looking up %1$s. Try again.
The server did not accept that address and password. Check them and try again.
Google did not accept that sign-in. Gmail does not allow your normal password in apps like Croft. Create an app password in your Google account and use that here.
Microsoft did not accept that sign-in. Outlook and Microsoft 365 do not allow your normal password in apps like Croft. Create an app password in your Microsoft account and use that here.
Apple did not accept that sign-in. iCloud needs an app-specific password, not your Apple ID password. Create one in your Apple ID account and use it here.
Fastmail did not accept that sign-in. Fastmail needs an app password, not your account password. Create one in your Fastmail settings and use it here.
The security certificate of %1$s was not issued by an authority Croft knows. Check the fingerprint before you trust it.
The security certificate of %1$s is not the one you trusted before. Check with the server\'s owner before you trust the new one.
Croft couldn\'t confirm that it is talking to your email provider at %1$s. Your password was not sent. Try another network.
The security certificate of %1$s is expired, made for another name or faulty. Ask the server\'s owner to fix it.
Couldn\'t connect to %1$s. Check the address, or try again.
%1$s does not offer a secure connection that Croft accepts, so Croft did not connect. Ask the server\'s owner to turn on current encryption (TLS 1.2 or newer).
%1$s answered but would not let Croft in. Try again later, or check the server\'s settings.
%1$s offers JMAP only. Croft can\'t sign in over JMAP yet. If the server also offers IMAP, enter its settings by hand.
The server settings can\'t be used. Check the server name, the port and the security setting.
Something went wrong inside Croft. Try again.
The server settings can\'t be used. Check the server name, the port and the security setting.
Croft can\'t use this server yet: it needs an IMAP server.
Croft lost the password before it could add the account. Type it again.
This device\'s Croft data was made by a newer version of Croft. Update Croft to add an account.
This address is already added, with different server settings. Remove that account first if you want to use these settings instead.
Something went wrong inside Croft while adding the account. Try again.
Croft couldn\'t open its secure storage on this device, so nothing was added. Try again.
Something unexpected went wrong. Nothing was added. Try again.
